To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we found non-cell-autonomy apoptosis and fewer ArxC interneurons in the neonatal neocortical of an X-linked ISS Arx expansion model, early estradiol therapy rescue ArxC interneuron density but did not prevent the apoptosis.
we identified a transient, non-cell-autonomous, non-innate immune, wave of elevated apoptosis and a reduction of Arx+ internes in neonatal neocoxtex of an X-linked ISSX model.
we identified a transient elevation in apoptosis in a mouse model for X-linked infantile spams syndrome, and that estradiol therapy does not diminish the elevated apoptosis in this model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathogenesis of X-linked infantilespasms syndrome and its treatment by estradiol.
the cellular mechanisms of X-linked infantilespasms syndrome and the early therapeutic effects of estradiol.
the pathogenic mechanisms underlying the most common triplet repeat expansion mutation of ARx, which is responsible for the devastating neurological disorder X-linked infantile spasm syndrome (ISSX).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Arx(GCG10+7) model of X-linked ISS syndrome is a useful tool to investigate the mechanisms underlying the disease.
the Arx expansion mutation perturbed cortical development by augmentating apoptosis without activating innate immune in a mouse model.
the early treatment with E2 in this model of X-linked ISS syndrome does not reduce apoptosis, but rescues the Arx+ cell numbers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found a transient wave of apoptosis that is non-cell-autonomous and not related to innate immune activation in the Arx(GCG)+7 model.
we found a transient increase in apoptosis that is non-cell-autonomous, and that is not targeted by estradiol or ACTH hormone therapy.
Arx(GCG10+7) mutation perturbs the development of the neocortex by increasing apoptosis without activating innate immune responses, and estradiol therapy rescues interneuron density in this model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
apoptosis in the neonatal cortex is a common pathogenic feature of Arx expansion models of ISSX.
early estradiol therapy may rescue cortical interneuron density in X-linked infantile spams syndrome, a developmental epileptic encepalopathy.
the augmented cell death in this mouse model of infantile spasms is non-cell-autonomous and not mediated through innate immune pathways.
